A Digital-First Approach to Land Management The cornerstone of this reform is the complete digitalisation of the allotment process. BIADA will now manage all plot and shed allotments exclusively through a public online portal where available land parcels will be listed transparently. This shift aims to eliminate discretionary practices and improve accountability in industrial development. Simplified Timelines The policy promises a more investor-friendly environment with predictable schedules for project approvals and industrial setup. BIADA has been directed to maintain the following allocation ratios within industrial zones: 55–65% for industrial plots. 15–25% for road infrastructure. 10–33% for green and open spaces. Final Take By introducing long-term lease models of 30, 60, and 90 years with renewal provisions, the government is attempting to provide long-term security for investors and manufacturers planning major capital expenditure. The policy represents more than an administrative reform. It signals Bihar’s intention to position itself as a serious industrial destination operating under a transparent and rules-based framework. Under the leadership of Samrat Chaudhary, the state is banking on these reforms to drive manufacturing expansion, attract private investment, and generate employment opportunities. For an economy historically dependent on agriculture, this industrial land policy reflects a broader vision for a more diversified, digital, and competitive Bihar.
